title: Add UI input + display for the per-trade personal strategy tag -- PositionIn/Out.strategy and ClosedTradeOut.strategy have zero frontend consumer
description: Filed by the frontend-backend-feature-gap-audit task. `strategy` (Elder ch. 55/56/58/59's personal, named strategy/setup tag -- his own examples: 'false breakout with a divergence,' 'pullback to value') exists on `PositionIn`, `PositionOut`, and `ClosedTradeOut` (backend/app/api/schemas.py) and is fully implemented backend-side across three already-`done` tasks (`backend-trade-strategy-tagging` plus two followups covering free-text-vs-fixed-list scoping, merge/overwrite semantics on re-adding the same ticker, and whitespace normalization) -- but grep confirms zero production frontend usage anywhere: the only hits for `strategy` outside `frontend/src/api/types.ts` are in `frontend/src/features/methodology/data/methodologyContent.ts`, which only prose-describes the Elder methodology, never reads a live API field. Concretely: `AddPositionDialog.tsx` has a free-text input wired to `PositionIn.entry_notes` but no equivalent input for `strategy` at all, so a user can never actually set this field through the UI, ever; `TradeJournalPanel.tsx` (the closed-trades table) has a 'Notes' column reading `entry_notes` but no 'Strategy' column reading `ClosedTradeOut.strategy`; `PositionsTable.tsx` has neither. This is a complete, previously-untracked UI gap for an entire Elder-methodology feature end-to-end, not a cosmetic single field -- for contrast, both `entry_notes` and `follow_up_notes` each got their own matching frontend task filed alongside (or shortly after) their backend counterpart (`frontend-trade-journal-entry-notes`, `frontend-trade-journal-followup-review`); `strategy` never did, and its own backend task's checklist never mentions a frontend consumer either (its own explicit scope note, 'not the Apgar or equity-curve features themselves', is about those two specific downstream features, not about basic UI input/display).

checklist.step: Add a free-text 'Strategy' input to AddPositionDialog.tsx (PositionIn.strategy), following entry_notes' own trim-and-omit-if-blank convention rather than inventing a new one.

Display PositionOut.strategy somewhere a held position's own entry_notes-equivalent context is already surfaced (PositionsTable.tsx and/or HeldPositionBanner.tsx -- check both for the closest existing precedent and decide).
Add a 'Strategy' column to TradeJournalPanel.tsx (ClosedTradeOut.strategy), matching the existing Notes column's em-dash-when-absent convention.

Decide whether strategy is offered as a free-text input only (matching entry_notes) or also as a 'recent tags' autocomplete/suggestion list sourced from the user's own prior strategy values (Elder's own framing: strategies are personal and evolve over time, so a fixed predefined list was already rejected by the backend task) -- record the decision and rationale either way.
MetricHelp/explanatory copy if warranted; tests + Storybook stories for any new/changed components; confirm the 90% coverage gate still holds.

decisions.decision: AddPositionDialog's new Strategy field (checklist item 1) uses the exact same trim-and-omit-if-blank convention entry_notes already established: a plain controlled text value trimmed at submit time, and the `strategy` key is omitted from the POST body entirely (not sent as an empty string) when the trimmed value is blank.
decisions.rationale: The checklist explicitly calls for mirroring entry_notes' own convention rather than inventing a new one, and the backend already strips/normalizes a blank-or-whitespace-only `strategy` to null either way (backend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups), so omitting the key client-side is purely a request-payload-shape nicety consistent with entry_notes, not a correctness requirement.

decisions.decision: PositionOut.strategy (checklist item 2) is displayed as a new 'Strategy' column on PositionsTable.tsx (plain text, em dash when absent, sortable since the raw field is a plain comparable string) -- NOT as a field on HeldPositionBanner.tsx. Grepping both files first confirmed neither currently displays `entry_notes` for a held position at all (only TradeJournalPanel's closed-trade rows show `entry_notes`, via the NotesCell/InfoBalloon pattern) -- so there was no literal existing entry_notes precedent in either file to mirror; this decision is based on which file is the better conceptual fit instead.
decisions.rationale: PositionsTable is the open-position analog of TradeJournalPanel (the closed-trade table), and this same task's checklist item 3 adds a matching 'Strategy' column to TradeJournalPanel -- giving both tables a symmetric Strategy column keeps the Elder ch. 55/56/58/59 per-trade tag visible consistently across a position's whole lifecycle (open and closed), rather than showing it in one place for open positions and a different place for closed ones. HeldPositionBanner.tsx was considered (it already surfaces a held position's entry context: Entry Price/quantity/date, Stop, Profit Target, in a per-ticker box layout on the Stock Detail page) and would also have been a defensible home, but it's scoped to one ticker at a time and already duplicates information available on the Portfolio page's own PositionsTable for that same ticker -- adding Strategy there too would be redundant with the PositionsTable column rather than filling a genuine gap. `strategy` was rendered as plain text (not TradeJournalPanel's NotesCell icon-plus-InfoBalloon pattern) in both tables because it's a short personal named tag by design (Elder's own examples are short phrases like 'pullback to value,' not paragraphs the way `entry_notes` can be) -- an expandable-detail affordance would be unnecessary UI weight for a value that's almost always short enough to render inline.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 4: `strategy` is offered via a freeSolo MUI `Autocomplete` (not a plain `TextField`) on AddPositionDialog, with its suggestion list ('recent tags') sourced from the distinct, non-null `strategy` values on the user's own *currently-held* positions -- derived client-side in PortfolioPage from `usePortfolio()`'s own already-fetched data (a `useMemo` over `portfolioQuery.data.positions`, passed down as a new `recentStrategies: string[]` prop), not from a new backend endpoint and not from `GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades`.
decisions.rationale: Checked what data is actually available before deciding, per this checklist item's own instruction: grepping backend/openapi.json confirms there is no endpoint returning distinct prior `strategy` values, so a 'recent tags' feature necessarily means either a new backend endpoint or a client-side derive from already-fetched data -- a new endpoint was rejected as unwarranted scope expansion for a plain distinct-values convenience list with no server-side computation of its own (no aggregation, filtering, or cross-user concern), especially since the exact same effect is achievable entirely client-side. A freeSolo Autocomplete (rather than a fixed, predefined dropdown) was chosen specifically because the backend-trade-strategy-tagging task already rejected a fixed list, since Elder's framing is that strategies are personal and evolve over time -- freeSolo preserves the ability to type any new value while still nudging reuse of an exact prior tag (which matters because the field groups by exact string match for the future ch. 59 'equity curves segmented by strategy' idea), which is exactly the UX the backend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups task's own `decisions` entry anticipated ('a suggest-from-existing-values autocomplete UX in a future frontend task is preferable precisely because it also preserves the trader's original casing for display while still nudging them toward reusing an existing tag'). An earlier revision of this implementation also unioned in `GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades`' own strategy values (calling `useClosedTrades()` directly from PortfolioPage, reusing the same queryKey TradeJournalPanel already uses) for a more complete 'every prior value, not just currently-held ones' list -- this was reverted after it broke several unrelated, timing-sensitive PortfolioPage tests (e.g. a position link resolving in both PositionsTable and RiskPanel earlier than a prior assertion expected, and the Trade Journal table appearing before an 'empty portfolio -> no table' assertion ran) by starting that fetch at the page's own mount instead of only once TradeJournalPanel itself later mounts further down the tree. Scoping to held positions only avoids that blast radius entirely, at the acknowledged cost of not suggesting a strategy that was only ever used on a now-closed trade -- a real but narrower gap than the regression risk of changing this page's query-start timing, and one a future task could close (e.g. by having AddPositionDialog pull the closed-trades list itself only once actually opened, rather than PortfolioPage prefetching it unconditionally) if the gap turns out to matter in practice.

decisions.decision: No MetricHelp popover was added for `strategy` anywhere (checklist item 5's 'if warranted' qualifier). Plain helper text was added only on AddPositionDialog's new field ('Your own named setup for this trade, e.g. \'pullback to value\' (Elder ch. 55/56/58/59)'), matching the existing Notes field's own helper-text convention.
decisions.rationale: MetricHelp exists to explain a computed metric's formula and interpret a specific numeric/categorical value for the user (e.g. buy/sell/trade grade percentages, the Stop/Profit Target figures) -- `strategy` is the opposite case: a personal, free-text label the trader themselves chooses and already understands the meaning of, with nothing computed or formulaic to explain. Adding a MetricHelp popover here would be explaining the user's own words back to them. This is also feature-component placement work (AddPositionDialog.tsx, PositionsTable.tsx, TradeJournalPanel.tsx, PortfolioPage.tsx all stayed feature-local under features/portfolio/ or pages/ -- no new components/common/ component was introduced by this task, since the Strategy cells reuse plain text/em-dash rendering already inline in each table rather than a new reusable component, and the Autocomplete is MUI's own library component, not a new app component needing its own Storybook story per Frontend.md §4's common/-only requirement).

comments.summary: Non-blocking: frontend/src/pages/PortfolioPage.test.tsx has pre-existing tests that implicitly depend on async query-start/resolution timing rather than asserting against deterministic DOM state. Independently reproduced during this review by re-adding a top-level useClosedTrades() call to PortfolioPage (the PR's own earlier, reverted revision) to union closed-trades' strategy values into recentStrategies: this breaks 'shows a loading state, then the equity stat cards and positions table' ('Found multiple elements with the text: AAPL' -- PositionsTable's and TradeJournalPanel's own AAPL both resolve by the time a bare screen.getByText('AAPL') runs) and 'shows the empty state when the portfolio has no positions' (queryByRole('table')).not.toBeInTheDocument() implicitly assumes TradeJournalPanel's own closed-trades query, whose default MSW fixture is non-empty, simply hasn't resolved yet). This confirms the task-worker's own account of why the closed-trades union was reverted -- it's a genuine, pre-existing test-fragility problem, not a cover story, and scoping this PR's recentStrategies to held-positions-only (the decisions entry for checklist step 4) is a legitimate way to sidestep it rather than a feature cut forced for no reason. Filed as frontend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups checklist item 1.

Non-blocking: the resulting behavior gap (a strategy used only on a now-closed trade is never offered as a recentStrategies Autocomplete suggestion) is real but narrow in practice -- acknowledged in the task's own decisions entry. Filed as frontend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups checklist item 2.

review.notes: Full review pass. Backend suite: 1618 passed, 99.94% coverage (unchanged by this PR -- no backend files touched). Frontend suite: 1060 passed across 101 files, 99.78% statements / 99.06% branches / 99.84% functions / 99.81% lines, all well above the 90% gate; every touched file at or near 100%. ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc/profit-target-wording-guard all clean. scripts/validate_tasks.py: 0 violations (387 tasks after adding this PR's own followups task). Cross-checked the MSW mock's overwrite-on-merge strategy semantics (tests/mocks/handlers.ts) directly against backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py's add_position handler (lines ~636-647) and its docstring (~919-933): both overwrite an existing strategy outright on an incoming non-empty value and leave it untouched when the incoming value is absent/empty -- matches exactly, unlike entry_notes' append semantics which the mock correctly keeps separate. Confirmed the Strategy field's trim-and-omit-if-blank convention genuinely matches entry_notes' own established convention (both omit the POST key entirely when the trimmed value is blank; done-task frontend-trade-journal-entry-notes' own decisions entry for entry_notes is the precedent, reproduced faithfully here). Storybook: correctly untouched -- no stories added or removed, consistent with Frontend.md §4 (AddPositionDialog/PositionsTable/TradeJournalPanel/PortfolioPage are all feature components, and no new components/common/ component was introduced; the Autocomplete is MUI's own library component, not an app component needing a story). Placement check (step 7a): no concerns -- all touched/changed code stayed feature-local under features/portfolio/ or pages/, no near-duplicate of an existing common/ component, no feature-component masquerading as common/. No backend route/schema changes, so backend/openapi.json correctly wasn't touched. Live browser walkthrough (Playwright script driving a locally started make dev stack against the real backend/dev sqlite db, since no Playwright MCP tool was available this session): added a position with a Strategy tag through the dialog, confirmed it rendered correctly in both the Positions table's and (after waiting for it) Trade Journal's new Strategy columns, confirmed the Autocomplete offered the just-used tag as a suggestion on reopening the dialog, no console errors, no failed/4xx+ network requests. Cleaned up by deleting the test position directly from backend/fintrade.db (not via the UI's close flow, which would have spuriously added a closed_trades row) -- verified back to the original 18 positions / 20 closed trades afterward. Also ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e): all 28 specs across dashboard/navigation/portfolio/stock-analysis/watchlist passed, no regression. All four recorded decisions entries are well-formed (decision + rationale, alternatives considered and rejected) and consistent with what's actually implemented; the one checklist item phrased as 'decide X' (step 4) has a matching decisions entry. The two non-blocking findings above are tracked on frontend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups (new task, depends_on this one) rather than only living in this PR comment.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-verified: backend 1618 passed/99.94% coverage and frontend 1060 passed/101 files/99.78% statements (exact match to pr-reviewer's numbers), ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean, e2e 28/28. Skimmed the full diff; confirmed the MSW mock's overwrite-on-merge strategy semantics against backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py lines 636-647 directly (matches). Independently reproduced the key scrutiny point by re-adding a top-level useClosedTrades() call to PortfolioPage.tsx (fixing the response-shape bug in the original reverted revision, which read a non-existent `.trades` instead of ClosedTradesResponse's actual `.items`) and confirmed it still breaks the same two PortfolioPage tests pr-reviewer found, for the same pre-existing query-ordering-fragility reasons -- not a feature cut. Live-browser spot-check against the real dev backend: added a position with a Strategy tag through the dialog, confirmed PositionsTable's Strategy column rendered it immediately, confirmed TradeJournalPanel's Strategy column (header present, em dash for rows without a tag, 20 rows intact) after the slow cold-cache live-price fetches finished, confirmed the Autocomplete suggested the just-used tag on reopening. backend/fintrade.db restored to 18 positions / 20 closed trades afterward. Agree with pr-reviewer's non-blocking scope call: held-positions-only recentStrategies is acceptable to ship now rather than folding the closed-trades union (and the pre-existing test-determinism fix it requires) into this PR -- the core gap (zero frontend consumer for strategy) is fully closed either way, and both findings are already tracked on frontend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups.
